initialReview.synthesisedAnswer: Passes through the proximal interosseous membrane into the anterior leg, descends with the deep fibular nerve and continues as dorsalis pedis at the ankle.
Somatic sensation: dorsal nerve of the clitoris (pudendal nerve). Autonomic cavernous fibres regulate erection.
Spiral bony labyrinth with about 2.5 turns around the modiolus; contains the cochlear duct between scala vestibuli and scala tympani.
No major branches in the neck before dividing into the internal and external carotid arteries.
Complete ring of hyaline cartilage: narrow anterior arch and broad posterior lamina. The only complete cartilaginous ring of the airway.
Motor nucleus in the pons. The motor root and nervus intermedius (sensory and parasympathetic fibres) emerge at the pontomedullary junction.
Emerges between the pyramid and olive of the medulla, exits through the hypoglossal canal and runs anteriorly to the tongue.
Increases mucosal surface area and airflow turbulence to warm, humidify and filter inspired air.
Ascends to the right of the abdominal aorta, grooves the posterior liver and passes through the diaphragm at T8 to enter the right atrium.
Returns venous blood from below the diaphragm to the right atrium, including blood from the lower limbs, pelvis, kidneys and liver.
Ascends in the carotid sheath without neck branches; enters the carotid canal, traverses the petrous temporal bone and cavernous sinus, then enters the subarachnoid space.
Near the carotid bifurcation, lies posterolateral to the external carotid artery. Its petrous segment lies anterior to the middle ear.
Compresses the crus of the penis or clitoris, reducing venous outflow to help maintain erection.
Crus of the penis or clitoris and adjacent tunica albuginea.
Descends in the infratemporal fossa, receives chorda tympani and passes close to the mandibular third molar; loops beneath the submandibular duct in the floor of the mouth.
Increases mucosal surface area and directs airflow; overlies the middle meatus and its sinus drainage pathways.
Female pelvis: vesicouterine pouch between bladder and uterus; rectouterine pouch (pouch of Douglas) between uterus and rectum. Male pelvis: rectovesical pouch between bladder and rectum.
Passes behind the first part of the duodenum, then ascends in the hepatoduodenal ligament posterior to the hepatic artery and bile duct.
Supplies triceps, anconeus, brachioradialis and the wrist/finger extensors through its deep branch and posterior interosseous nerve. No intrinsic hand muscles.

Radial groove injury: wrist/finger extension weakness and dorsolateral hand sensory loss, with triceps largely spared. An isolated superficial branch lesion causes sensory symptoms without motor weakness.
Female: posterior to the uterus and vagina, with the rectouterine pouch above. Male: posterior to the bladder, seminal vesicles and prostate.
Divides into upper, middle and lower lobar bronchi; the upper lobar bronchus arises above the pulmonary artery (eparterial).
Central skull-base bone contributing to the orbits and cranial fossae; the pituitary sits in its hypophyseal fossa (sella turcica).
Somatic sensation from the face, cornea, teeth, oral/nasal cavities and much of the cranial dura; general sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue via V3.
Forearm: flexor carpi ulnaris and medial half of flexor digitorum profundus. Hand: most intrinsic muscles, including interossei, medial two lumbricals, hypothenar muscles and adductor pollicis.

Weak finger abduction/adduction and thumb adduction (Froment sign), medial 1½-digit sensory loss and ulnar clawing. Elbow lesions may also weaken FCU/FDP; Guyon’s canal lesions can spare dorsal hand sensation.
Female: passes beneath the uterine artery near the cervix (water under the bridge). Male: passes beneath the ductus deferens before entering the bladder.
Calculi can lodge at ureteric narrowings. During hysterectomy, the ureter is at risk where it passes beneath the uterine artery.
In females, passes inferoanteriorly from the bladder neck through the pelvic floor to open in the vestibule.
In females, lies anterior to the vagina and is closely related to its anterior wall.
Behind the pubic symphysis. Female: anterior to the uterus and vagina. Male: anterior to the rectum, with seminal vesicles and ductus deferens ampullae intervening.
Supplies most palate, pharynx and larynx muscles; carries parasympathetic fibres to thoracoabdominal viscera.
Travels through the internal acoustic meatus with CN VII and enters the brainstem at the cerebellopontine angle.

mergedReview.synthesisedAnswer: Axons of retinal ganglion cells; the optic nerve is part of the central nervous system.
Damage before the chiasm causes visual loss in the same eye; asymmetric damage can cause a relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD).
Vocal-fold movement: recurrent laryngeal nerve. Cricothyroid tensioning: external branch of superior laryngeal nerve. Sensation below the folds: recurrent laryngeal nerve.
